description.short_caption: Axial chest CT showing pleural effusion and lung consolidation.
description.detailed_description: This axial chest CT image shows a large pleural effusion on the left side, with the fluid appearing as a homogenous, low-density area. The adjacent lung parenchyma demonstrates consolidation with increased density, suggesting possible infection or inflammation. The right lung appears aerated with no obvious abnormalities. The mediastinum is midline, and the bony structures appear intact.

description.short_caption: Chest radiograph showing bilateral pulmonary infiltrates.
description.detailed_description: This is a frontal chest radiograph showing the thoracic cavity. There are bilateral patchy opacities predominantly in the mid and lower lung fields, consistent with pulmonary infiltrates. The cardiac silhouette appears normal in size, and there is no obvious pleural effusion or pneumothorax. The bony structures, including the ribs and clavicles, appear intact.

description.short_caption: Histopathology with fungal elements stained using a special stain.
description.detailed_description: This image shows a histopathological section stained with a special fungal stain, likely Gomori methenamine silver (GMS) or a similar technique. The fungal elements are highlighted in dark brown or black, contrasting against a blue-green background. The fungal morphology includes round to oval structures, consistent with yeast forms. The surrounding tissue appears to have cellular detail, suggesting an inflammatory response.
